headline: Araghchi seven-day Hormuz initiative
dek: Araghchi told Al Ekhbariya TV that Washington had accepted Tehran's conditions for a seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz but sought additional provisions (unspecified). Indirect Iran-US contacts continue via mediators in Pakistan and Qatar.
sources: Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi (Oct 21 interview with Iraq's Al Ekhbariya TV); corroborated proposal history via AP, Reuters, Gulf News, UN stakeout recording Sept 25
fault_line: Can Iran's day-6 reopening promise be trusted as diplomacy — or is Hormuz leverage until the last sanctioned barrel clears? Who blinks first: Washington's blockade or Tehran's strait?

sections.what_happened: Araghchi told Al Ekhbariya TV that Washington had accepted Tehran's conditions for a seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz but sought additional provisions (unspecified). Indirect Iran-US contacts continue via mediators in Pakistan and Qatar. Under the plan: initial US steps (4-5 days), full Hormuz reopening on day six, final-agreement talks on day seven. The US side has NOT confirmed his account. Trump said Sept 26 'I reject their proposal.' Iran wants the US to fulfill Islamabad-memorandum commitments first; Vance (Oct 5) demands 'meaningful' reduction in uranium enrichment. EIA: Hormuz-related Middle East crude shut-ins averaged 4.8M bpd in September. IEA: Hormuz flows measured 10.9M bpd in September (+3.7M vs August).
sections.what_verified: AP (plan terms), Reuters (Oct 18 recording: plan on table, Iran reviewing US comments), Gulf News (Baghdad/OIC remarks), UN stakeout recording
sections.what_disputed: No US official has confirmed 'accepted conditions'; Trump Sept 26: 'I reject their proposal'; Vance Oct 5: deal needs meaningful enrichment reduction — a sequencing demand Iran rejects
sections.why_matters: Hormuz by the Numbers: 4.8M barrels/day shut in (EIA), 10.9M/day flowing (IEA), and a day-six promise only Washington can unlock. Put the day-by-day sequence on screen with the price. The question: is the US buying time for the third carrier or buying the deal?
sections.context: Background: Araghchi seven-day Hormuz initiative — claims Washington 'accepted conditions but wants additions'; indirect talks via Pakistan and Qatar continue
